extracted.intended_audience: shippers/carriers/packaging designers, radiation safety officers, regulatory compliance officers, and other stakeholders in radioactive materials transport
extracted.subtask_description: Final-rule guidance revising the Hazardous Materials Regulations (HMR) to harmonize with IAEA TS-R-1 (1996) and related international/ISO standards for transport of Class 7 (radioactive) material, including numerous definitional, labeling, marking, packaging, and transport-control requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consignment definition clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the definition of "consignment" to address shipments of bulk containers (e.g., gondolas, intermodals) by rail and other transport vehicles, distinguishing single railcar consignments from groups of railcars and accounting for differences in hazards between aircraft group shipments and multiple bulk containers on rail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule modifies the definition to resolve ambiguity about whether one railcar is one consignment or whether multiple railcars/gondolas constitute one consignment; justification cites differing hazard profiles by mode and configuration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance (QA) definition brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief, formal definition of "Quality Assurance" rather than enumerating specific personnel (health physicists, RSO, nuclear engineers, NRC/DOT personnel) or equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency disagrees with commenter asking for detailed wording; definition should be concise and not intended to set forth comprehensive QA program elements (those remain in program requirements elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: IAEA TI multiplication factor for large dimension loads (status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision whether to adopt the IAEA TS-R-1 multiplication factor for Transport Index (TI) for large dimension loads is deferred; the proposed rule does not include the IAEA factor, maintaining an incompatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOT acknowledges the IAEA guidance and will continue to analyze whether the multiplication factor should become a U.S. requirement; current variations may reflect cost/benefit, risk-informed rulemaking, and stakeholder comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of import-use prerequisite for foreign Type A packaging (§173.415(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete the requirement that a foreign-made Type A packaging must have first been 'used for the import of Class 7 materials' before it may be used for domestic or export shipments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retained requirement was unnecessary and ran counter to harmonization intent; final rule eliminates that prerequisite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wipe efficiency definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Define "wipe efficiency" as the fraction of removable contamination that is taken up by a wipe and counted as a sample, not as the efficiency of the counting instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying this distinction (with a parenthetical definition) eliminates confusion in applying §173.443; default wipe efficiency of 0.10 may be assumed when true wipe efficiency is not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Out-of-scope comment handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments proposing broad operational or policy changes (e.g., dedicated vehicles, mandatory escorts, banning air shipments, escort inspections at state lines, personnel restrictions) are outside the scope of this rulemaking and will not be considered here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of exemplar comments provided; agency only addresses issues within the regulatory scope of harmonization with TS-R-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update incorporated references to TS-R-1 and select ISO standards (Part 171)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace/revise references to older IAEA Safety Series No.6 and DOE/ISO documents with IAEA "Regulations for the Safe Transport of Radioactive Material, No. TS-R-1, 1996 Edition" and add two ISO standards plus a U.S. Enrichment Corporation guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table of material incorporated by reference is adjusted for harmonization and to include relevant ISO and industry standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use TS-R-1 definition of radioactive material across HMR and ICAO consistency (§171.11, §171.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt the TS-R-1 definition of Class 7 (radioactive) material for domestic and international shipments so both the HMR and ICAO Technical Instructions use the same definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes former duplicative internal definitions and aligns domestic and international transport thresholds and terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology change: 'limited quantities' → 'excepted packages' (§171.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Change phrasing in §171.11(d)(6)(iii) and (iv) from 'limited quantities' to 'excepted packages' to clarify applicability to instruments, articles, empty packagings, and limited quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that exceptions apply to items such as instruments or articles containing natural uranium or thorium and to empty packagings as well as certain excepted packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise Hazardous Materials Table entries for Class 7 (Part 172 §172.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise radioactive material (Class 7) entries in the Hazardous Materials Table to be consistent with new UN Recommendations and TS-R-1, and remove entries that previously allowed domestic-only shipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harmonizes shipping names and entries with international standards and reduces domestic-only deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shipping paper entry simplification and CSI requirement (§172.203)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove redundant shipping-paper requirements (entering 'Radioactive Material' and LSA/SCO group notation), require customary units enclosed in parentheses if used, remove Pu-238 from list of fissile radionuclides for weight listing, and require Criticality Safety Index (CSI) be included in the shipping description for fissile material packages. Move 'Highway route controlled quantity' wording to a separate paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplifies and modernizes shipping paper content and adds CSI to aid transport and emergency response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial packaging marking and country-of-design code (§172.310)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require industrial packagings to be marked 'Type IP-1,' 'Type IP-2,' or 'Type IP-3' as applicable, and require the outside of Type IP-2, Type IP-3 or Type A packaging to be marked with the international vehicle registration code of the country of origin of design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brings wording more into correspondence with TS-R-1 and improves traceability/identification of packaging design origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce FISSILE label and separate CSI/TI concepts (§172.400 et seq.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a new 'FISSILE' label for fissile material packages and introduce the Criticality Safety Index (CSI) as a distinct number separate from the Transport Index (TI) used for radiation control purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSI must be displayed on fissile material packages via the FISSILE label; TI continues for radiation hazard and is displayed on the radioactive material label. Decoupling improves clarity about which hazard the number refers to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to bear FISSILE label for fissile packages (§172.402)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require each package containing fissile material, other than fissile-excepted packages, to bear the new FISSILE label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistent labeling for identification of criticality hazard separate from radiation hazard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete FISSILE label with CSI and labeling flexibility for LSA-I (§172.403)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require each FISSILE label to be completed with the CSI. For LSA-I material, authorize entry of 'LSA-I' on RADIOACTIVE YELLOW II and YELLOW III labels as an alternative to listing radionuclides; require customary units in parentheses; add paragraph (h) incorporating §173.448(g) overpack-labeling requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds detail to ensure CSI is always present on the FISSILE label and provides labeling alternatives to simplify marking for LSA-I material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification for FISSILE label (§172.441)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a new §172.441 to identify specification requirements for the new 'FISSILE' label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a dedicated place for technical and sizing/spec requirements for the FISSILE label to ensure uniform implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Except items integral to transport vehicles from HMR (§173.401)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except from the HMR certain integral items such as thoriated metallic engine parts, depleted uranium counterweights, tritium exit signs, and similar items containing radioactive material that are part of, and routinely used in, the normal operation of a transport vehicle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also except certain natural materials/ores containing NORM under specified conditions, with an upper limit of 10× the activity concentration or consignment thresholds to keep worker/public doses small while allowing commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive revisions to §173.403 definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Add, remove, and revise numerous definitions (remove 'Non-fixed radioactive contamination' as standalone; revise A1/A2, Containment system, Exclusive use, Fissile material, LSA, Low toxicity alpha emitters, Maximum normal operating pressure, Multilateral approval, Package, Radioactive contents/material, Special form, SCO, TI, Unilateral approval, Unirradiated uranium, etc.). Add new definitions for Consignment, Contamination (including fixed/non-fixed), CSI, Deuterium, Exemption value, Fissile material package, Fixed radioactive contamination, Graphite, and Quality assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to align with TS-R-1, to clarify terms, to introduce CSI, and to ensure internal consistency across the HMR. Examples: remove Pu-238 from 'fissile material' and base exemptions on nuclide-specific (dose-based) approach rather than single specific-activity threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of 'Non-fixed radioactive contamination' and integration into 'Contamination'
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the separate definition and fold its essential elements into the definition of 'contamination' for clarity, aligning with Safety Series No.6 and TS-R-1 quantitative definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents inadvertent gaps that would leave materials with surface contamination below prior numeric levels unregulated; clarifies fixed vs non-fixed contamination concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of 'Fissile material' definition (remove Pu-238)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise 'fissile material' definition to be consistent with TS-R-1 and to include uranium-233, uranium-235, plutonium-239, plutonium-241 (or combinations), and remove plutonium-238 from the fissile definition because it is fissionable but not fissile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that definition refers only to fissile radionuclides themselves, not non-fissile material containing them; affects classification and handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: LSA-I definition revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise Low Specific Activity (LSA) material definitions (LSA-I) to allow shipments of very low specific activity materials containing various radionuclides and remove the prior category referencing mill tailings, contaminated earth, rubble, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns with TS-R-1 approaches and broadens clarity on what materials can be treated as LSA-I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport Index (TI) revision to TS-R-1 consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the Transport Index definition to be consistent with TS-R-1; TI remains the number used to provide control over radiation exposure and assigned to packages, overpacks, freight containers or unpackaged LSA-I/SCO-I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TI continues to describe radiation hazard while CSI will describe criticality hazard separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticality Safety Index (CSI) introduction and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce CSI as a definition and metric intended to simplify representation of a package's criticality hazard separate from its radiation hazard; CSI is displayed on packages of fissile material and used along with TI to aid shippers, carriers, and emergency responders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSI reduces uncertainty about whether a TI reflects radiation or criticality and allows TI to describe radiation only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption value definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'exemption value' to mean the activity concentration or consignment activity thresholds above which a material is sufficiently radioactive to be subject to the HMR, distinguishing it from DOT exemptions under §171.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies threshold terminology and its regulatory implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance (QA) definition added to HMR
rubrics_metrics.description: Add the TS-R-1 definition of Quality Assurance to the HMR to clarify what is meant by a QA program and to indicate that a NRC-approved program or adherence to §§173.474/173.475 is acceptable for certain exports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brings clarity to expectations for QA when issuing Certificates of Competent Authority and for packaging certification processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excepted packages are not excepted from all marking requirements (§173.421, §173.424, §173.426)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that excepted packages (including those containing limited quantities or instruments/articles containing radioactive material, and articles containing natural uranium/thorium) are not exempt from all marking requirements and in some cases must bear UN identification numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §173.422 eliminated prior certification-statement requirement but requires UN identification marking; active material in an instrument/article must be completely enclosed by non-active components; empty packages must also carry markings and protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excepted package marking and UN identification (§173.422, §173.428)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate the certification-statement requirement for excepted packages, require excepted packages to be marked with the UN identification number, and require empty packages to be marked with the UN ID and have uranium/thorium components covered by an inactive sheath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes outdated procedural certification while ensuring adequate marking and physical safeguards for empty shipments.

rubrics_metrics.name: LSA/SCO transportation and packaging clarifications (§173.427)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify LSA/SCO transportation and packaging requirements, prohibit fissile LSA (material containing fissile radionuclides may be classified as LSA only if it satisfies fissile-excepted conditions), clarify exclusive use provisions, and authorize transportation of unpackaged LSA-I and SCO-I material. Remove previous exception for 10 CFR 20.2005 materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets conditions under which low-specific-activity and surface contaminated objects may be transported and when exclusive-use controls apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt nuclide-specific exemption values and calculation rules (§173.433, §173.436)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference and adopt nuclide-specific exemption values (Table I of TS-R-1) and provide a new table for exempt material activity concentrations and exempt consignment activity limits; clarify how to calculate limits for mixtures and for Type A package contents involving special and normal form material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaces single uniform activity exemption (70 Bq/g) with more rigorous, dose-based, nuclide-specific approach; retains limited domestic exceptions (e.g., Mo-99 up to 20 Ci in Type A; Cf-252 values retained).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace A1/A2 values with TS-R-1 Table I values (§173.435)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the existing A1/A2 radionuclide values (and footnotes) with those from Table I of TS-R-1, keeping narrow domestic exceptions where noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns Type A package activity limits with international table values.

rubrics_metrics.name: True non-fixed contamination limits and wipe efficiency application (§173.443)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise Table 11 to list the true non-fixed contamination limits for package outer surfaces and revise paragraph (a)(1) to require that in calculating contamination from activity measured on a wipe, the true wipe efficiency must be used or a default efficiency of 0.10 may be assumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures contamination assessments use correct wipe uptake fractions; clarifies measurement practice to reduce misapplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce CSI-based transport controls for fissile packages (§173.447, §173.457, §173.459)
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate CSI concept and TS-R-1 CSI limits into rules simplifying fissile package transport requirements, eliminating the old 'fissile material, controlled shipment' construct, and replacing references to criticality control TI with CSI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since all fissile transport is limited by total CSI carried on a conveyance, previous special controlled-shipment procedures are no longer needed; total CSI conveyance limits provide adequate safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relocate overpack labeling requirements to §172.403(h) (§173.448)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove overpack-labeling requirements from §173.448(g)(1) and relocate them to §172.403(h) for logical organization and to aid the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidates labeling rules in part 172 to improve usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: UF6 packaging performance and approval changes (§173.420, §173.477)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce new performance packaging requirements for packagings containing more than 0.1 kg of UF6 and add a new §173.477 to define approval requirements for such packagings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies special performance and approval pathways for uranium hexafluoride packagings above a mass threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak-test and impact-test standard updates (§173.469)
rubrics_metrics.description: Update reference for alternate leak test methods from ISO/TR 4826-1979(E) to ISO 9978-1992(E), clarify leaching assessment application, and allow substitution of Class 4 impact test from ISO 2919-1980(E) for basic impact/percussion tests with TS-R-1 restriction that sealed capsule mass <200 g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modernizes referenced test standards and clarifies applicability and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: QA program content and pre-shipment action description requirement for certificates (§173.476)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify what the required quality assurance program should cover and add a requirement that a description of any planned pre-shipment actions for consignments of special form radioactive material be included in applications for U.S. Competent Authority Certificates for Special Form Material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fills a previous gap where TS-R-1 described QA expectations but HMR did not; ensures pre-shipment procedures are documented in certification applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rail and air CSI/TI carrier limits and exclusive-use rules (Parts 174–175 §§174.700, 175.700–703)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that an upper TI limit of 50 refers to both total TI and total CSI for non-exclusive use shipments by rail (§174.700); limit CSI to max 3.0 for a fissile package on passenger aircraft (§175.700) and require exclusive use for any package/overpack/consignment with CSI > 50 shipped by air; add cargo-aircraft-only requirements reflecting TS-R-1 separate limits (§175.702) and generalize fissile-air shipment requirements (§175.703).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure both radiation and criticality hazards are controlled in air and rail transport; specify when exclusive-use and special arrangements are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segregation and separation distances for fissile groups on vessels (§176.704) and rail (§176.700)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce additional transportation controls based on CSI, replace tables to list Transport Index Limits and Criticality Safety Index Limits, and require groups of radioactive material packages containing fissile material be separated by at least 6 m (20 feet) from other groups; emphasize that appropriate transport restrictions for fissile packages apply to rail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decouples segregation controls for radiation and criticality, provides numerical separation requirements, and supports alternate dose-rate-based segregation methods for exclusive-use shipments with an approved radiation protection program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate segregation method dose-rate guidance and exclusive-use restriction (§176.708)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide more detailed dose-rate guidance for an alternate method to determine segregation distances (per IMDG Code) and restrict the use of this alternate method to exclusive-use shipments for which a radiation protection program approved by the competent authority of the flag state of the vessel is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits application of alternative methods to situations with full radiation-protection oversight to maintain safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace many obsolete DOT specification authorizations and markings (Part 178 §§178.350–178.364)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove obsolete references/authorized use of various DOT specification packagings (6L, 6M, 6M/20WC/21WC, 20WC wooden jackets, 21WC overpacks) and revise marking requirements to remove duplicative wording and require DOT specification packagings be marked with manufacturer name/address or symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cleans up obsolete authorization of older packagings and clarifies marking responsibilities for DOT-spec packagings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory significance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule is not considered a significant regulatory action under Executive Order 12866 section 3(f) and was not reviewed by OMB; it is also not considered a significant rule under DOT Regulatory Policies and Procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rulemaking relied on NRC analyses (NUREG/CR-6713) and internal regulatory analyses to reach this determination.
